verdict: WITHIN-REACTION ARROWS: THE PREMISE WAS RIGHT, THE FIRST RULE WAS WRONG, AND THE FIX IS CATALYSIS. Orienting {A,B} from the reaction where A and B ACTUALLY interact is a better question than the global 'does some reaction containing A precede some reaction containing B'. But the obvious local rule -- A is an input, B is an output -- reaches almost nothing: of the 36,415 PPI edges (19.02%) whose endpoints share a reaction, only 95 split across input and output, while 1,593 are BOTH INPUTS. That is not a gap in the data, it is what binding IS: the reaction is A + B -> AB, both partners go in, and inside the step where two proteins bind, neither comes first. Reactome agrees in its own vocabulary -- the `category` breakdown of reactions containing a PPI edge is {'binding': 4288, 'transition': 2473, 'omitted': 697, 'dissociation': 327}. THE RELATION THAT CARRIES DIRECTION IS CATALYSIS. In a phosphorylation Reactome records input = {substrate, ATP}, output = {phospho-substrate, ADP} and the kinase as a CATALYST, so input->output yields substrate -> phospho-substrate (the same protein) and never recovers kinase -> substrate, which is the arrow SIGNOR actually records. TWO DATA FACTS HAD TO BE PROBED, AND EITHER WOULD HAVE WRECKED THIS SILENTLY. First, the catalyst entity is usually the whole ENZYME:SUBSTRATE complex, so expanding it fires both directions at once and the edge cancels to 'ambiguous'; Reactome's `activeUnit` names the subunit that actually acts, and preferring it is what makes the rule mean 'the enzyme acted on the product'. Second, the existing sym2pe map is keyed by DISPLAY NAME ('p-Y342-PTK6', not 'PTK6') and never expands complexes, so it was rebuilt here by recursing through hasComponent/hasMember to UniProt geneName. MEASURED: ALL orients 6,014 PPI edges (3.14%) at 0.8242 +/- 0.0171 on n=495; AU 3,603 edges at 0.7296 +/- 0.0214 on n=429; AU+MONO 221 edges at 0.8824 +/- 0.0391 on n=68. THE CONTROL THAT DECIDES IT is the degree rule ON THE SAME EDGES, because a random walk's direction on an undirected graph is provably the degree ratio and the annotation could simply be selecting edges where degree already works: 0.5535 / 0.5291 / 0.5000 respectively. The best stratum, AU+MONO, is 0.8824 against a matched 0.5000, so catalysis carries direction the graph's own shape does not. It also clears the global precedence rule's 0.6547. It orients 5,630 edges the global rule does not, so the two are complementary rather than redundant. WHAT THIS CANNOT SAY. Reactome describes canonical human biology, not K562. Reactome and SIGNOR curators read overlapping literature, so agreement between them is not fully independent validation. And the ceiling remains 78%: 'the direction of a PPI edge' is not single-valued, because protein-level and transcriptional direction on the same pair legitimately oppose.
